flags.headline: Q2 2026 earnings miss continues to weigh; 4th consecutive down session since the print
flags.detail: Monday 8/10 close: $9.55, -5.54% (vs Friday's $10.11), the 4th straight down session since Q2 2026 results on 2026-08-06 (net loss $611M/$1.60 per share vs. consensus for a $0.35 profit; revenue -27% YoY to $175M, with $343M of the loss from unrealized Bitcoin mark-to-market). Cumulative decline since the print is now roughly -20%. Countervailing signals this run: Rosenblatt reaffirmed a Buy rating with a $15 PT post-print; California State Teachers' Retirement System (CalSTRS) disclosed a new 78,842-share purchase (filed 8/9). Cantor Fitzgerald's $12 PT (cut from $14) and Morgan Stanley's $5.50 Underweight remain the bear case. No new negative catalyst found this run beyond continued price decay -- flagging as persisting, not escalating further.
flags.thesis_link: Direct hit on two MARA key_risks: 'Persistent GAAP losses...driven by Bitcoin price volatility and mark-to-market accounting create existential risk' and 'Revenue concentration in Bitcoin mining means MARA's financial performance is essentially a leveraged derivative of Bitcoin price.' This quarter is exactly that risk materializing.

flags.headline: Wildfire-liability-reform deadline now 20 days out (Aug 31); no draft legislation found
flags.detail: Monday 8/10 close unchanged materially from Friday. CEO Pedro Pizarro's warning stands: without a credit-supportive framework passed by California's legislature before the Aug 31 session end, SCE's already-lowest-investment-grade S&P rating likely gets downgraded into junk territory. This run's search still found no draft wildfire-liability-reform bill circulating -- the gap between the deadline and visible legislative progress is widening, not narrowing, as the window closes.
flags.thesis_link: Matches EIX key_risk: 'Elevated debt-to-equity of 216% amplifies financial risk from future wildfire events, adverse rate case outcomes, or rising interest rates.' A credit downgrade would directly worsen this exposure.

evidence.source: Seeking Alpha (Edison falls on deadline warning)

flags.headline: Reported talks to backstop $250B of OpenAI data-center funding; lost #1 market-cap spot to Apple
flags.detail: Monday 8/10 close: $219.16, -2.88% (vs $223.93 prior). Reports emerged that NVIDIA is in talks to backstop as much as $250B in funding tied to a major OpenAI data-center buildout -- a circular-financing structure (chip vendor financing its own customer's demand for its chips) that the market read negatively, with NVIDIA ceding its position as the world's most valuable company to Apple. Unconfirmed/talks-stage, not a completed transaction. Distinct from, but adjacent to, the AI-infrastructure sector sympathy weakness flagged separately below.
flags.thesis_link: Touches NVDA key_risk: 'AI capex sustainability risk...any normalization of hyperscaler spending could cause rapid growth deceleration.' A vendor-financed circular-demand structure raises questions about the quality/durability of the capex NVDA is counting on, though this is a market-sentiment read on an unconfirmed deal, not a confirmed demand shortfall -- kept at AMBER pending confirmation or terms.

flags.headline: AI-chip sector sympathy weakness: SK Hynix -14%, Samsung -13% abroad; ASML hit on China chip-equipment competition report
flags.detail: Monday 8/10 close: $209.00, -4.56% (vs $218.63). No MRVL-specific news found -- move tracks a broader semiconductor sell-off following a sharp decline in South Korean and Taiwanese chip names (SK Hynix >14%, Samsung >13%) plus a report that a Chinese state-backed company began mass-producing key chipmaking equipment, which hit ASML and reignited China-competition and AI-capex-quality (circular financing) concerns sector-wide. This is the standing hyperscaler-capex/AI-infrastructure watch item materializing as sector-wide sympathy pressure, not a company-specific break.
flags.thesis_link: Touches MRVL key_risk: 'Forward P/E of 53.3x...any miss against the $16.5B FY2028 revenue target or moderation in hyperscaler AI capex would trigger severe multiple compression.' Sector-wide, not company-confirmed -- AMBER.

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance (Micron, SK Hynix stocks sink as AI chip sell-off deepens)
